content.text: {"steps":[{"id":"s1","description":"Use list_documents, then read candidate_specs.md and any detector-upgrade or RPC-design documents that define candidate gas mixtures, GWP100 values, allowed assumptions, or simulation settings. Extract the three candidate mixture definitions and their GWP100 values."},{"id":"s2","description":"Apply the hard environmental constraint: keep only candidate mixtures with GWP100 <= 150 and exclude any candidate above 150 from all further consideration. Record each retained candidate's GWP100 as a numeric result where possible."},{"id":"s3","description":"For every retained candidate mixture, run simulate_time_resolution at gas gaps spanning the allowed 1 to 3 mm range, including at least 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5, and 3.0 mm. Record each returned time resolution in ns as a numeric result."},{"id":"s4","description":"Identify the best-performing region from the initial scan for each retained mixture. Around each apparent minimum, run additional simulate_time_resolution calls with finer gap spacing, staying within 1 to 3 mm, to refine the optimum time resolution. Record the refined time-resolution values."},{"id":"s5","description":"Compare all compliant mixture-gap combinations using the simulated time resolution as the primary objective, verify the selected gas gap is within 1 to 3 mm and the selected mixture has GWP100 <= 150, and provide the reporting module with the single lowest-time-resolution compliant mixture and gap."}]}
